title: Version-anchoring orchestrator with progressive traffic shift and safety guards
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We need a deterministic, safe way to anchor sessions to a model version during progressive rollouts (canary / A-B) while preserving latency SLOs, minimizing cache misses across variants, and providing automated fallback to compatible variants when capacity or quality issues arise. Existing route resolvers either (a) indiscriminately pin by session causing long-lived imbalance, or (b) use purely probabilistic splits that lose session affinity and KV cache locality.

Goal: Implement a Version-Anchoring Orchestrator that performs: (1) incremental traffic graduation (0% -> 100%) to anchored versions using cohort-based ramps, (2) deterministic session anchoring with TTL and graceful graduation, (3) safety gates (SLO, error, quality) that automatically throttle or rollback shifts, and (4) variant-aware fallback scoring so that requests degrade to compatible model variants in the same geo/tier before falling back to higher-latency remote tiers.

Non-goals: Full rollout UI work (Console UX will be tracked in a follow-up PM ticket); replacing existing persistent routing store — we will extend it conservatively.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic anchoring: sessions assigned to anchor cohorts should consistently route to the same model version for the configured TTL unless a forced migration happens.
Progressive ramp: traffic can be ramped with cohort sizes configurable (e.g., 1%, 5%, 20%) and ramps respect burst/bucket limits.
Safety gates: automated gates pause or shrink the ramp when p95 latency increases > 25% over baseline, or error-rate > 0.5% absolute, or quality-DRIFT alert triggers.
Fallback policy: when an anchored variant is unavailable, requests first try geo/tier-compatible variants, then the next tier, preserving region preference when possible.
KV-cache warming: the orchestrator provides hooks to notify serving runtime to pre-warm KV caches for newly promoted cohorts within 60s of ramp start.
Observability: dashboards show cohort membership, per-cohort latency/error/quality, and a single control to abort or roll back a ramp to previous allocation.
E2E tests: deterministic suite proving anchor TTL expiry, cohort graduation, and fallback ordering under simulated node failures.
implementation_plan: Design state machine for cohort lifecycle: PENDING -> ACTIVE -> DRAINING -> EXPIRED
Extend route resolver: add 'version_anchoring' policy with deterministic hashing + session salt + TTL override
Cohort manager service: new lightweight service that emits cohort assignments and publishes cohort delta events to routing-proxies
Safety gate service (leverage existing SLO service): evaluate moving windows and produce actions (throttle, pause, rollback)
Fallback scorer module: compute candidate variants ordered by compatibility score (arch, quant, seq-len, latency profile)
KV cache warm API: small endpoint for runtime to accept warm-up hints and return readiness status
Integrations: publish schema changes to routing config and add config migration script for existing pinned routes
PRs: split into 4 PRs - cohort manager, resolver updates, fallback scorer, safety gate integration
testing_plan: Unit tests for deterministic anchoring hashing and TTL behavior
Integration test: simulated multi-variant cluster with node failures to validate fallback ordering
Load test: ramp cohorts under traffic profile derived from production percentiles to measure p50/p95 token latency impact
Chaos test: randomly kill variant pools during a ramp and assert automatic rollback within configured tolerances
Quality regression test: run small eval suite on canary traffic to detect model-output drift before increasing cohort
E2E CI job: run on every PR with mocked safety gate signals to validate cutover actions
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - internal dogfood: enable for < 0.5% traffic on staging clusters for 72h
Phase 1 - limited production: enable for 1% cohorts on non-critical customer routes for 48h; monitor gates
Phase 2 - wider production: ramp cohorts to 10% across traffic buckets over 7 days with automated gating
Phase 3 - general availability: allow self-serve cohort configurations in Console with guardrails; default TTL=24h
Abort and rollback: single-call rollback endpoint that immediately marks cohorts DRAINING and rebinds sessions to prior version
Communication: release notes + runbook for SREs and solutions engineers with playbook for manual intervene
